title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon, retakes the frontier-benchmark lead
subtitle: The new model writes up to 1 million tokens per response, posts the lowest hallucination rate of any frontier system, and leads outright on 12 of 18 benchmarks against GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on September 30 as its new frontier model. Across 18 benchmarks Google disclosed, Argon leads outright on 12 and ties for first on one, while GPT-6 Astra leads on three and Claude Opus 5.5 leads on two. On LVBench, a long-video understanding test, Argon posted 91.7%. On the Harvey legal-agent benchmark, Argon scored 19.6% to GPT-6 Astra's 5.4%. On the AA-Omniscience evaluation, Argon registered a 15% hallucination rate — the lowest of any model in its tier, versus 51% for GPT-6 Astra. Argon can also write up to one million tokens in a single response. API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output. Initial access goes to Google AI Ultra subscribers, paid API customers, and a Fairwind cohort of vetted cyber defenders.

The headline is the hallucination number. 15% is not a solved problem, but it is a step change in a category where every lab has been stuck between 40 and 55 for most of the year. If it holds up outside Google's own evaluation harness, it tightens the gap between what a frontier model can plausibly draft and what a human can ship without a verification pass. The 1-million-token output ceiling is the second architectural shift: it changes what a single call can produce — a full research memo, a complete codebase refactor, a transcript analysis across hours of video — without a stitching layer on top. Pricing undercuts GPT-6 Astra at both the input and output ends.

This lands two days after OpenAI pulled GPT-6.1 Astra over safety-eval failures, and one day after Anthropic's leaked IPO filing. The frontier is now a three-way race where each lab has a different weakness exposed: OpenAI's shipping discipline, Anthropic's valuation posture, and until today, Google's benchmark position. Argon re-centers Google in the leaderboard conversation while the Fairwind-first rollout — defenders before enterprise before consumer — reads as a direct response to the FTC probe opened the same day over AI-agent safety behavior.

For learners: hallucination rate is the metric to watch more carefully than any 'reasoning' benchmark right now. A model that answers correctly 85% of the time and refuses the other 15% is a different tool from one that fabricates 50% of its unknowns with confidence. If you're evaluating a frontier model for your own work, run the AA-Omniscience protocol on it, or something like it, before you trust its citations. The capability gap between labs on reasoning is narrowing; the gap on calibration is where the real work still is.
